fr.elements: Main Building; Secondary Building; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Road; Internal Drive Aisle; Open Green Space; Dense Vegetation; Landscaped Area; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Multiple Structures; Limited Rear Access; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations: Ensuring the single access point and extended driveway remain unobstructed at all times could significantly improve emergency responder approach and egress, particularly given the presence of multiple structures on the property. Posting visible address markers near the primary access point and along the internal drive aisle may assist responders in navigating between the main building, secondary building, and detached structure more efficiently. Preserving adequate turning and staging space within the vehicle parking area or open green space would support apparatus positioning and operational deployment. Where dense vegetation borders the driveway or internal drive aisle, maintaining clearance along those travel corridors could improve responder movement and visibility throughout the property.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Dense Shrub Cover; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Fuel Continuity; Heavy Ground Vegetation; Brushland Interface; Long Driveway; Limited Defensible Space; Scattered Trees
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing the density of brush in direct contact with the structure and creating greater separation between shrub masses and building surfaces could meaningfully reduce fuel continuity and improve defensible space around the improvements. Where vegetation is growing immediately adjacent to exterior walls, foundations, or under eaves, thinning or removing that material would reduce the opportunity for surface fire to reach the structure. Managing the heavier ground vegetation and creating horizontal spacing between remaining shrub clusters could interrupt continuous fuel pathways across the property. Along the driveway, maintaining cleared margins on both sides would support firefighter access and improve evacuation visibility given the length of the approach route. Addressing areas where mixed and dense shrub cover transitions close to the structure perimeter, and maintaining separation between the tree cluster and adjacent shrub masses below, could further reduce vertical fuel continuity and support suppression operations over the long term.
